candidate.attack: Check the bramble conditions on arbitrary G by constructing the family and proving the hitting-set lower bound; also verify the upper bound via the doubling-bag construction.
candidate.definitions: G[K_2] = lexicographic product of G with K_2; vertices (v,i) for v∈V(G), i∈{0,1}; (a,i)~(b,j) iff a~b or (a=b and i≠j).
candidate.derivation: 1. Let 𝔅 be a bramble of G of order q = tw(G)+1 (Seymour-Thomas). 2. In H = G[K_2] the set {B×{i} : B∈𝔅, i∈{0,1}} is connected because each B×{i} induces a copy of G[B]. 3. If B and B' touch in G, then B×{i} and B'×{j} share a vertex or have an edge in H, and B×{0} and B×{1} are adjacent via edges (a,0)-(a,1). 4. Any hitting set X of this family must satisfy |X_i| ≥ q for each i, hence |X| ≥ 2q, so the bramble order is at least 2q and tw(H) ≥ 2q-1 = 2·tw(G)+1. 5. The standard doubling-bag upper bound replaces each bag X_t by X_t×{0,1}, yielding width 2·tw(G)+1. Hence tw(G[K_2]) = 2·tw(G)+1 exactly.
candidate.known_closest: The general identity tw(G[K_n]) = n(tw(G)+1)−1 for lexicographic products with cliques K_n is stated in the literature (e.g., Bodlaender 1998) but not verified for K_2.
candidate.novelty: Provides a bramble-based constructive proof for the lower bound tw(G[K_2]) ≥ 2·tw(G)+1 and combines it with the standard doubling-bag upper bound to establish exact equality.
candidate.obstacle: Verify that the family {B×{i} : B∈𝔅, i∈{0,1}} satisfies the bramble conditions (connectedness, touching) in H and that any hitting set X must have size at least 2(tw(G)+1) for arbitrary G.
candidate.target_relevance: Closes the lower-bound part of the width-theorem obligation S0018, which requires proving tw(G[K_2]) ≥ 2·tw(G)+1 for all G.

statement: Thm 4.1, Thm 5.4, Cor 6.2 of the owner's paper (as stated there). PAPER SETTING: G=(V,E) finite graph, F field, K subspace of F^I, blocks I_v; pi_X: K -> prod_{v in X} F^{I_v}. (R) rank pi_X >= d|X| for all X subset V; (L) z,z' in K with z|v != 0 != z'|v => supp z cap supp z' != empty; (E) uv in E, z|u != 0, z'|v != 0 => supports intersect. text: Corrected form of the S-NEW-DEPTH observation (replaces the overclaim that the unfolded formula has superpolynomial size). Let N=2^m, s=m^c, c>=1, and let D_dec be the depth of the decision circuit built by the S0020 construction, with D_dec <= D + C*s*log2(m+s) + C*log N. Unfolding that circuit into a tree gives a formula of size at most 2^(D_dec+1). For s=m^c this upper bound is 2^(omega(m)) = N^(omega(1)) for every c>=1. This is an UPPER bound from depth only. Theorem 1.3 is the streaming theorem: if search-MCSP^A[s(n)] (s(n) >= n, A in PH, N = 2^n) has no 1-pass deterministic poly(s(n))-space streaming algorithm with poly(s(n)) update time, then P != NP. The abstract states the same. Theorem 1.4 is the circuit-depth theorem (TC0, NC1, P/poly), not the streaming one. So contract row C's 'Thm 1.3' is correct and the owner note's 'Thm 1.4' is wrong for this statement. def CycSat (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : Nat → Nat, (∀ j, j < n → a j ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ i, i < n → a (i % n) + a ((i + 1) % n) + a ((i + 2) % n) = 1

theorem cyc13_sat_iff_three_dvd (n : Nat) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : CycSat n ↔ 3 ∣ n := by
  unfold CycSat
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨a, ha01, hsum⟩ := h
    apply Classical.byContradiction
    intro hnd
    have hpos : 0 < n := by omega
    have hall : ∀ m, a (m % n) + a ((m + 1) % n) + a ((m + 2) % n) = 1 := by
      intro m
      have := hsum (m % n) (Nat.mod_lt _ hpos)
      simp only [Nat.mod_mod, Nat.mod_add_mod] at this
      exact this
    have hper : ∀ x, a ((x + 3) % n) = a (x % n) := by
      intro x
      have h0 := hall x
      have h1 := hall (x + 1)
      rw [show x + 1 + 1 = x + 2 by omega, show x + 1 + 2 = x + 3 by omega] at h1
      omega
    have hstep : ∀ m, a ((m + 1) % n) = a (m % n) := by
      intro m
      have hshift : ∀ k, a ((m + 3 * k) % n) = a (m % n) := by
        intro k
        induction k with
        | zero => simp
        | succ k ih =>
          rw [show m + 3 * (k + 1) = (m + 3 * k) + 3 by omega, hper, ih]
      obtain ⟨k, t, hkt⟩ : ∃ k t : Nat, 3 * k = 1 + t * n := by
        have h3 : n % 3 = 1 ∨ n % 3 = 2 := by omega
        rcases h3 with h | h
        · exact ⟨2 * (n / 3) + 1, 2, by omega⟩
        · exact ⟨n / 3 + 1, 1, by omega⟩
      have e : (m + 3 * k) % n = (m + 1) % n := by
        rw [show m + 3 * k = (m + 1) + t * n by omega, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_right]
      rw [← e]
      exact hshift k
    have hc : ∀ j, a (j % n) = a (0 % n) := by
      intro j
      induction j with
      | zero => rfl
      | succ j ih => exact (hstep j).trans ih
    have h0 := hall 0
    have e1 := hc (0 + 1)
    have e2 := hc (0 + 2)
    omega
  · intro hd
    refine ⟨fun j => if j % 3 = 0 then 1 else 0, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro j _
      dsimp only
      split <;> omega
    · intro i _
      simp only [Nat.mod_mod_of_dvd _ hd]
      split <;> split <;> split <;> omega

#print axioms cyc13_sat_iff_three_dvd

text: UNREVIEWED LEMMA (author family claude-haiku, same as this session; needs review by another model family before any use as a premise). STATEMENT: G a graph, c: V->{0,1} with sum_v c(v) even. T(G,c) is the CNF with, for each vertex v, one clause per local edge-assignment at v of parity != c(v); clause width = deg v. Let m = min{deg v : c(v)=1}. CLAIM: every resolution refutation of T(G,c) contains an initial clause of width >= m. PROOF: let x be the all-zero edge assignment. The clause at v forbids a local assignment of parity 0 when c(v)=1, so x falsifies it; x falsifies a clause only if c(v)=1, and then its width is deg v >= m. Suppose every initial clause of a refutation P has width < m. Then x satisfies every initial clause of P. Resolution preserves satisfaction by the fixed assignment x: if x satisfies C or y and D or not-y, then x satisfies C or D (if x(y)=1 it satisfies D, otherwise C). So x satisfies every clause of P, including the empty clause, a contradiction. SCOPE: GF(2) Tseitin CNF only; width only, no size bound. For G=K_n and c = indicator of one vertex, m = n-1. NOT claimed as new: this is a standard one-sided width argument for Tseitin formulas. CONSISTENCY: measured minima K3=2, K4=4, K5>=7 (cm-88c97aad7b8449b6, cm-235f5acd28484ce4) satisfy the bound. It says nothing about the GF(3) kernel encoding F(K_n) of Q-33e33ccf08, and it closes no named obligation (G0001, G0005 untouched). S0003 and S0004 remain CLAIMED.

Theorem 1.3: if some time-constructible s(n) >= n and A in PH make search-MCSP^A[s(n)] unsolvable by a poly(s(n))-space streaming algorithm with poly(s(n)) update time, then P != NP (proof: P = NP answers the Sigma3SAT^A calls of Thm 1.2).
